source.original_text: For a real symmetric matrix A in a finite Euclidean space, let F(x)=xᵀAx on the induced unit sphere. Its Riemannian gradient vanishes exactly when Ax=⟨x,Ax⟩x. Therefore a unit stationary vector is an eigenvector, and conversely every unit eigenvector is stationary; its eigenvalue equals⟨x,Ax⟩.

∀ {E : Type u_1}
  [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (n : ℕ)
  [inst_3 : Fact (Module.finrank ℝ E = n + 1)] (A : E →L[ℝ] E),
  (↑A).IsSymmetric →
    ∀ (x : ↑(Metric.sphere 0 1)),
      ((d% fun y => inner ℝ (↑y) (A ↑y)) x = 0 ↔ A ↑x = inner ℝ (↑x) (A ↑x) • ↑x) ∧
        ((d% fun y => inner ℝ (↑y) (A ↑y)) x = 0 ↔ ∃ μ, Module.End.HasEigenvector (↑A) μ ↑x)

blind_reconstruction.text: Let E be a finite-dimensional real normed inner-product space of dimension n+1, where n is any natural number, and let A:E→E be a continuous real linear symmetric operator. Give the unit sphere S={x∈E:‖x‖=1} its n-dimensional sphere manifold structure, and define f:S→ℝ by f(y)=⟨y,Ay⟩. Let Df(x) be the manifold derivative used by the Lean statement, totalized to zero outside differentiability. For every x∈S, both of the following equivalences hold: Df(x) is the zero linear map if and only if Ax=⟨x,Ax⟩x; and Df(x) is the zero linear map if and only if there exists a real scalar μ such that Ax=μx and x≠0. Thus the zero-differential condition at the chosen unit vector is equivalent to that vector being an eigenvector, with its eigenvalue given by the quadratic value ⟨x,Ax⟩.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.SphereGradient
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Rayleigh

/-!
# Rayleigh objectives on the unit sphere

Boumal Example 3.62: the induced gradient of the literal sphere restriction
of a symmetric quadratic is its projected ambient gradient. Critical points
are exactly unit eigenvectors. The pairing uses the actual sphere inclusion
differential; it does not replace the induced metric by a chart metric.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.SphereRayleigh

open Metric InnerProductSpace
open scoped Manifold InnerProductSpace

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]

/-- The concrete Rayleigh vector is the unique ambient tangent representative
of the genuine sphere differential with the inclusion-induced pairing. -/
theorem sphere_rayleigh_characterization
    (n : ℕ) [Fact (Module.finrank ℝ E = n + 1)]
    (A : E →L[ℝ] E) (hA : A.IsSymmetric) (x : sphere (0 : E) 1) :
    ∀ z : (ℝ ∙ (x : E))ᗮ,
      ((∀ w : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x,
        mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x w =
          ⟪mvfderiv (𝓡 n) ((↑) : sphere (0 : E) 1 → E) x w, (z : E)⟫_ℝ) ↔
        (z : E) = (2 : ℝ) • (A (x : E) - ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E))) := by
  have hx : ‖(x : E)‖ = 1 := mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.mp x.property
  have hg : HasGradientAt (fun y : E => ⟪y, A y⟫_ℝ) ((2 : ℝ) • A (x : E)) (x : E) := by
    apply hasGradientAt_iff_hasFDerivAt.mpr
    have hraw := (hA.hasStrictFDerivAt_reApplyInnerSelf (x : E)).hasFDerivAt
    have hfun : (fun y : E => ⟪y, A y⟫_ℝ) = A.reApplyInnerSelf := by
      funext y
      simp [ContinuousLinearMap.reApplyInnerSelf_apply, real_inner_comm]
    have hlin : toDual ℝ E ((2 : ℝ) • A (x : E)) =
        (2 : ℕ) • innerSL ℝ (A (x : E)) := by
      ext v
      simp [toDual_apply_apply, two_smul]
    rw [hfun, hlin]
    exact hraw
  let K := (ℝ ∙ (x : E))ᗮ
  have hproj (u : E) : (K.orthogonalProjectionOnto u : E) =
      u - ⟪(x : E), u⟫_ℝ • (x : E) := by
    change (ℝ ∙ (x : E))ᗮ.starProjection u = _
    rw [Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal_val,
      Submodule.starProjection_unit_singleton ℝ hx]
  have hp : (K.orthogonalProjectionOnto ((2 : ℝ) • A (x : E)) : E) =
      (2 : ℝ) • (A (x : E) - ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E)) := by
    rw [hproj]
    simp [inner_smul_right, smul_sub, smul_smul]
  intro z
  rw [SphereGradient.sphere_gradient_characterization n x hg z]
  constructor
  · intro hz
    exact (congrArg (fun v : K => (v : E)) hz).trans hp
  · intro hz
    apply Subtype.ext
    exact hz.trans hp.symm

/-- Genuine sphere stationarity is equivalent both to the Rayleigh-coefficient
equation and to actual eigenvectorhood; unit membership supplies nonzeroness. -/
theorem sphere_rayleigh_stationary_iff
    (n : ℕ) [Fact (Module.finrank ℝ E = n + 1)]
    (A : E →L[ℝ] E) (hA : A.IsSymmetric) (x : sphere (0 : E) 1) :
    (mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x = 0 ↔
      A (x : E) = ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E)) ∧
    (mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x = 0 ↔
      ∃ μ : ℝ, Module.End.HasEigenvector A.toLinearMap μ (x : E)) := by
  have hx : ‖(x : E)‖ = 1 := mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.mp x.property
  have hxne : (x : E) ≠ 0 := by
    intro hz
    simp [hz] at hx
  have hzero := sphere_rayleigh_characterization n A hA x 0
  have hd :
      mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x = 0 ↔
        A (x : E) = ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E) := by
    have he :
        mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x = 0 ↔
          ∀ w : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x,
            mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x w = 0 := by
      constructor
      · intro h w
        rw [h]
        rfl
      · intro h
        ext w
        exact h w
    rw [he]
    have hs : (0 : E) = (2 : ℝ) •
        (A (x : E) - ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E)) ↔
          A (x : E) = ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E) := by
      rw [eq_comm, smul_eq_zero, sub_eq_zero]
      simp
    have hpair :
        (∀ w : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x,
          mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x w = 0) ↔
          (0 : E) = (2 : ℝ) • (A (x : E) - ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E)) := by
      simpa only [Submodule.coe_zero, inner_zero_right] using hzero
    exact hpair.trans hs
  refine ⟨hd, ?_⟩
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact ⟨⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ,
      Module.End.mem_eigenspace_iff.mpr (hd.mp h), hxne⟩
  · rintro ⟨μ, hμ⟩
    have hAx : A (x : E) = μ • (x : E) := hμ.apply_eq_smul
    have hcoef : ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ = μ := by
      rw [hAx, inner_smul_right]
      simp [hx]
    apply hd.mpr
    rw [hcoef]
    exact hAx

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.SphereRayleigh

candidate_publication_context.statement: For a real symmetric matrix A, let F(x)=xᵀAx on the unit sphere with the metric induced by the Euclidean inner product. The chosen smooth ambient quadratic extension has gradient2Ax. The tangent projector sends u to u−⟨x,u⟩x, so the sphere gradient is2(Ax−⟨x,Ax⟩x). Its vanishing is equivalent to Ax=⟨x,Ax⟩x; thus the stationary unit vectors are exactly eigenvectors of A, and every unit eigenvector is stationary.

formulae.label: Unit tangent projector and gradient
formulae.tex: P_xu=u-\langle x,u\rangle x,\qquad \operatorname{grad}_S F(x)=2(Ax-\langle x,Ax\rangle x).

formulae.label: Both directions of stationarity
formulae.tex: \operatorname{grad}_S F(x)=0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ Ax=\langle x,Ax\rangle x\ \Longleftrightarrow\ x\text{ is a unit eigenvector of }A.

assumptions: Finite-dimensional real Euclidean space, real symmetric matrix A and a unit vector x.
Unit sphere with the metric induced by the ambient inner product; F(x)=xᵀAx, the sphere restriction of the smooth quadratic extension.

obligations.label: Construct the actual restricted differential and its unique induced tangent representative, with explicit formula2(Ax−⟨x,Ax⟩x).
Zero actual differential iff the Rayleigh-coefficient equation iff actual unit eigenvectorhood, including the converse.

lesson.title: Sphere stationary points are exactly unit eigenvectors
lesson.statement: For the same symmetric quadratic on the induced unit sphere, the genuine manifold differential at x is zero exactly when Ax=⟨x,Ax⟩x, and exactly when x is an eigenvector of A. If Ax=μx, the unit norm forces μ=⟨x,Ax⟩. Zero or negative eigenvalues are allowed.
lesson.formula: DF(x)=0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ Ax=\langle x,Ax\rangle x\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \exists\mu\in\mathbb R:\ Ax=\mu x,\ x\ne0,\qquad Ax=\mu x\Rightarrow\mu=\langle x,Ax\rangle.
assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space of dimension n+1. In orthonormal coordinates A is the source real symmetric matrix; its continuous-linear-map representation adds no regularity assumption in finite dimension.
A is symmetric, not necessarily positive, positive definite or invertible. x has norm one. Nonzeroness of x and the Rayleigh eigenvalue identity are derived internally, not added hypotheses.

The objective is the literal sphere restriction F(x)=⟨x,Ax⟩ of the smooth quadratic q(y)=⟨y,Ay⟩. The ambient quotient is defined only for y≠0; its equality with this restriction uses ‖x‖=1. No derivative of an off-domain totalized quotient is used.

The metric is the ambient-induced one. The actual inclusion derivative Jₓ maps abstract chart directions into x⊥. Pairings with Jₓw express this induced metric explicitly; no default chart inner product is identified with it.

n may be zero. The claims are pointwise, with every x and every tangent test direction quantified. They neither construct a global gradient-field object nor claim a convergence or extremal-eigenvalue theorem.

steps.title: Turn zero differential into zero projected gradient
steps.text: A continuous linear differential is zero exactly when it vanishes on every tangent direction. The first theorem at the candidate z=0 says that these vanishing pairings hold precisely when Gₓ=0. This explicitly implements the source-derived bridge from differential stationarity to induced-gradient stationarity. Cancel the nonzero real scalar2 and rearrange the difference.
steps.formula: DF(x)=0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ DF(x)[w]=0\ \forall w\ \Longleftrightarrow\ 0=2(Ax-\langle x,Ax\rangle x)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ Ax=\langle x,Ax\rangle x.

have hx : ‖(x : E)‖ = 1 := mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.mp x.property
  have hxne : (x : E) ≠ 0 := by

  have hzero := sphere_rayleigh_characterization n A hA x 0
  have hd :
      mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x = 0 ↔
        A (x : E) = ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E) := by
    have he :
        mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x = 0 ↔
          ∀ w : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x,
            mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x w = 0 := by
      constructor
      · intro h w
        rw [h]
        rfl
      · intro h
        ext w
        exact h w
    rw [he]
    have hs : (0 : E) = (2 : ℝ) •
        (A (x : E) - ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E)) ↔
          A (x : E) = ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E) := by
      rw [eq_comm, smul_eq_zero, sub_eq_zero]
      simp
    have hpair :
        (∀ w : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x,
          mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x w = 0) ↔
          (0 : E) = (2 : ℝ) • (A (x : E) - ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E)) := by
      simpa only [Submodule.coe_zero, inner_zero_right] using hzero
    exact hpair.trans hs
steps.detail: The proof uses extensionality of the actual differential, not an arbitrary supplied pairing identity. The characterization tests every chart direction through the canonical induced pairing. Norm one gives x≠0 internally.

steps.title: A stationary unit vector is an eigenvector
steps.text: The preceding equality puts x in the eigenspace with eigenvalue ⟨x,Ax⟩. Unit membership proves x≠0, so this is genuine eigenvectorhood in the library sense rather than the equation alone, which would also hold at zero.
steps.formula: Ax=\langle x,Ax\rangle x,\quad\|x\|=1\Rightarrow x\ne0,\qquad x\in E_{\langle x,Ax\rangle}(A)\setminus\{0\}.
steps.lean:
refine ⟨hd, ?_⟩
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact ⟨⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ,
      Module.End.mem_eigenspace_iff.mpr (hd.mp h), hxne⟩
steps.detail: Module.End.mem_eigenspace_iff supplies eigenspace membership; HasEigenvector includes the proved nonzeroness. No spectral existence theorem or positivity assumption is needed.

steps.title: Every unit eigenvector is stationary
steps.text: Conversely, suppose Ax=μx. Pair with x to get ⟨x,Ax⟩=μ‖x‖²=μ. Thus the eigenvector equation is exactly the Rayleigh-coefficient equation, and the first equivalence gives DF(x)=0. This proves the converse for any real eigenvalue, including zero and negative values.
steps.formula: \langle x,Ax\rangle=\langle x,\mu x\rangle=\mu\|x\|^2=\mu,\qquad Ax=\langle x,Ax\rangle x\Rightarrow DF(x)=0.
steps.lean:
· rintro ⟨μ, hμ⟩
    have hAx : A (x : E) = μ • (x : E) := hμ.apply_eq_smul
    have hcoef : ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ = μ := by
      rw [hAx, inner_smul_right]
      simp [hx]
    apply hd.mpr
    rw [hcoef]
    exact hAx
steps.detail: HasEigenvector.apply_eq_smul gives the actual eigenvalue equation. The coefficient identity uses the source unit norm; it is not added as a theorem hypothesis.

lesson.lean_statement: The first conjunct identifies a zero continuous-linear-map differential with the Rayleigh equation. The second conjunct identifies it with an existential actual Module.End.HasEigenvector. All x on the unit sphere are quantified, and no nonzero-eigenvalue premise is present.
lesson.lean_proof: Evaluate the genuine gradient characterization at zero; derive the coefficient equation; construct the actual eigenvector and prove the converse by unit normalization.
